subject: Computer Networking
title: WebRTC: Browser-to-Browser
description: Learn WebRTC: Browser-to-Browser in one minute.

hook.text: You open a link and video chat starts — no app install, no plugin. WebRTC makes that happen in the browser.

buildup.text: WebRTC provides real-time audio, video, and data channels directly between browsers using JavaScript APIs.

discovery.text: It negotiates the best path: direct peer-to-peer when possible, through a relay server when firewalls block.

twist.text: Despite being peer-to-peer, WebRTC still needs a signaling server to help peers find each other initially.

climax.text: Google Meet, Discord calls, and many telehealth apps all use WebRTC for real-time communication.

punchline.text: WebRTC turns every browser into a video phone.

quiz.question: What does WebRTC enable?
options: Real-time audio and video directly in the browser
Faster HTTP downloads for large files

details.summary: WebRTC enables peer-to-peer audio, video, and data communication directly between browsers without requiring plugins or server relay for media. It uses STUN and TURN servers for NAT traversal, DTLS for encryption, and adaptive bitrate algorithms to handle varying network conditions in real time.
details.whyItMatters: WebRTC powers video calls, screen sharing, and file transfer directly in the browser. It eliminated the need for plugins like Flash, making real-time communication accessible on every device.
takeaways: WebRTC connects browsers directly for peer-to-peer media
STUN and TURN servers help traverse NATs and firewalls
All WebRTC media is encrypted with DTLS and SRTP by default

faq.question: How does WebRTC work through firewalls?
faq.answer: WebRTC uses ICE to find connectivity paths. STUN servers help peers discover their public IP addresses. If direct connection fails due to restrictive NATs, TURN servers relay media traffic through a server. Most connections succeed with STUN alone; TURN is the fallback for about 15 percent of cases.

faq.question: Does WebRTC always send data directly between peers?
faq.answer: WebRTC tries peer-to-peer first, which works in most cases. When both peers are behind restrictive firewalls, a TURN relay server forwards the traffic. For group calls with many participants, SFU servers receive and distribute streams more efficiently than full mesh peer connections.
